title: Sums commute with a mapped pointwise bound
statement:
Let $f\colon\alpha\to\bbn$, $g\colon\beta\to\bbn$, and $h\colon\alpha\to\beta$ be functions into the natural numbers, let $cs$ be a finite list of elements of $\alpha$, and let $k\in\bbn$. If $g(h(c)) \le k\, f(c)$ holds for every entry $c$ of $cs$, then, summing over the entries of $cs$ (with multiplicity),
\[ \sum_{c \in cs} g\bigl(h(c)\bigr) \;\le\; k \sum_{c \in cs} f(c). \]
hypotheses_covered: functions f, g into the naturals and h between the domains
cs a finite list over the source type
pointwise bound g(h c) ≤ k · f c for every entry c of cs
replaced:
A technical lemma: if $g(h\,c) \le k \cdot f\,c$ for all $c \in cs$, then the additive
\texttt{foldr} of $g$ over $cs.\mathrm{map}\;h$ is at most $k$ times the additive
\texttt{foldr} of $f$ over $cs$.
